questions.question:
**Choose the best substitute for the bracketed segment in the following sentence to complete the sentence meaningfully.**

(No sooner did she shouted), than the thieves ran away leaving all the jewellery on the table.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **No sooner did she shout**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The use of "**shouted**" in the original sentence is grammatically incorrect because the past tense marker "**did**" already **indicates the tense**, and we use the base form of the verb after it.
 
• "**No sooner**" is a **correlative conjunction** that is used in conjunction with "**than**" to express that one action or event happens immediately after another.
 
• The correct past tense usage after "**No sooner**" is the **simple past tense**.
 
 
• **Example**: *No sooner did the students finish their exams than they began planning a celebratory trip.*
 
 
 
• In this case, "**did she shout**" is the correct form, where "**did**" is **an auxiliary verb** used for emphasis in a past tense sentence, and "**shout**" is the **base form of the verb.**
 
• Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *No sooner did she shout, than the thieves ran away leaving all the jewellery on the table.*
 
• This construction ensures proper grammar and maintains the intended meaning of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

When Mayank came, / I shall go / with him to / the circus.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **When Mayank came**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The error in the original sentence is in the **verb tense agreement**.
 
• The issue is that the past tense "**came**" in this segment conflicts with the use of the future tense "**shall go**" in the following segment.
 
• In this case, "**comes**" is appropriate.
 
• This suggests that whenever "**Mayank comes**" as a regular occurrence or in the future.
 
• In conditional statements, especially those **expressing future conditions**, use "**comes**" in the **if-clause** to indicate a possible future event.
 
• So, the **correct sentence** would be: *When Mayank comes, I shall go with him to the circus.*

Thus, **option 2** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the following sentence in active voice.**

A play is being staged by our group this evening.

options.text: A play staged our group this evening.
Our group stages a play this evening.
Our group is staging a play this evening.
Our group staged a play this evening.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Our group is staging a play this evening.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the passive voice.
 
• To convert it to active voice, we need to **identify the subject performing the action** and rearrange the sentence accordingly.
 
• In **passive **voice, **the focus is often on the action or the result** rather than the person or thing performing the action.
 
• **Passive structure**: Object + to be + V3 + Subject__
 __
 
• **Example**: *A new bridge is being built by them.*
 
 
 
• **Active structure**: Subject + Verb + Object__
 
 
• **Example**: *They are building a new bridge.*
 
 
 
• Here, In the active voice transformation, the **subject **"**our group**" is moved to the beginning of the sentence.
 
• The tense of the verb becomes "**is staging**" (**present continuous**) in the active voice.
 
• The active voice version is more direct and clearer. It explicitly states that "**our group**" is the one **performing the action** of staging a play.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.

• "**As well as**" is a comparative phrase used to compare the abilities, qualities, or characteristics of two or more things.
 
 
• **Example**: *The new employee works as well as the experienced ones.*
 
 
 
• It is commonly used to indicate that one person or thing possesses a certain quality to the same degree or in a similar manner as another.
 
• Therefore, the corrected sentence should use "**as well as**" to compare the dancing abilities.
 
• **Corrected sentence**: *I don’t think he can dance as well as Elena.*
 
• In the context of the sentence the phrase "**as well as**" is **used to compare the dancing abilities of "he" and "Elena."** 

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.
